title: Cue Stack Onramp — sketch
content:
Objective:
Quick sketch of a lightweight user onramp for shipping small, structured context items ("cues") into Redwood requests with minimal token overhead. Goal is to make it trivial for product teams to attach high-value, compact context (preferences, little facts, task hints, verification cues) that get selectively merged into prompts at inference time without bloating sessions.

Problem statement:
- Users need to provide small bits of context repeatedly (e.g., role: "legal adviser", tone: "concise", product IDs, user preferences).
- Putting everything into long instruction blocks or full session history inflates token usage and increases latency/cost.
- Teams want a first-class UX and API to manage these micro-context items: versioning, preview, fallback, and partial merging.

Hypothesis:
If we provide a "Cue Stack" onramp (UI + API + runtime hints) that stores and transmits compact cues and enforces merging policies at the runtime, teams can reduce average per-request tokens by 20–40% for contextual-heavy features while improving editability and predictability of the prompt envelope.

Key concepts / primitives:
- Cue: a small named key/value or structured snippet (text, JSON-lite)
- Stack: ordered list of cues applied to a request; can be global (per-organization), per-user, or per-session
- Merge policy: how and where cues are placed (prefix, suffix, template slot, metadata-only, tool-arg)
- Compression profile: rules that compress cues (abbrev, enums, canonicalization) to reduce tokens
- TTL / ephemeral: cues can be persisted long-term or marked ephemeral for single-request use

User journeys (rough):
1) New product onboards: creates cue templates in Console -> examples (name: "role", type: enum, synonyms) -> product dev attaches stack id to route config.
2) End user flow: app sends stack-id + overrides (e.g., "role=manager") -> runtime merges with request using merge policy and sends to model.
3) Debugging: dev opens Console -> selects a request trace -> sees applied cues (expanded + compressed form) and toggle to inspect expanded prompt.

API sketches:
- POST /cue-stacks -> create stack (name, scope, default cues, merge policy)
- GET /cue-stacks/{id} -> metadata + cue list
- POST /requests?stack_id=xxx -> request-level overrides: {overrides: [{k,v}], ephemeral: true}
- Runtime hint header: X-Redwood-Cue-Profile (compact|full|meta-only)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: create/edit/delete stacks, basic preview (how prompts will look with 2 sample templates)
- API: create stack + attach to request; request with overrides merges predictably and shows up in trace logs
- Runtime: support prefix/suffix/template-slot merge policies; compressed representation that is <50 tokens for typical stacks of 4 cues
- Telemetry: per-request token delta reported (with/without cues) and error rates when merging fails

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 10 internal teams try Cue Stack in staging
- average token reduction per request for adopters >= 15%
- no runtime PU (production-unique) incidents caused by merging logic; errors < 0.1% of requests
- Console time-to-create-stack < 5 minutes for new user

Risks & open questions:
- Semantic collisions: cue names that conflict with prompt variables or tool args. Need namespace scoping and safe escaping.
- Quality regressions: compressed cues may remove nuance and alter outputs. Need micro-evals per adoption.
- Privacy/PII: cues persisted at org/user scope may contain sensitive info; need KMS labels and redaction in traces.
- Compatibility with multi-model fallback (different models expect cues in different formats).

Experiment plan (fast follow):
- A/B: route 10% of requests for a single product through Cue Stack with compressed vs raw-inlined contexts; measure cost, latency, and output quality via evaluation prompts.
- Small internal hackathon: three teams build integrations (email assistant, search re-ranker, onboarding wizard) to validate broad applicability.

Console UX notes (brainstorm):
- Quick-create modal with suggested cue types (role, tone, product_id, locale, user_pref)
- Preview toggle: compact -> expanded -> final prompt; shows token count delta live
- Stack library: shareable stacks with tags + owner + change history
- Safe edit: rollback/preview diffs and "dry run" toggle to test endpoints without impacting production quota

Runtime implementation sketch (engineering notes):
- Store cues as compact protobuf-like records in route metadata store, serve with a small signed manifest per request to avoid large payloads
- Merge engine: deterministic template engine (must be idempotent), apply per-request overrides with strict typing
- Introduce a middleware stage that calculates token delta and applies compression heuristics before hitting compilation/kernels

Telemetry and observability:
- Traces: log applied stack id, expanded cue set (redacted), token delta, merge error codes
- Metrics: cue_stack_adoption, cue_stack_token_savings_total, cue_stack_merge_errors

Rollout strategy:
- Alpha: internal teams + trusted customers (feature flag) for 6 weeks
- Beta: opt-in in Console, more templates and per-route suggestions
- GA: default library + migration guides for customers who inline context today

Next actions (today):
- Talia: write short RFC skeleton and link to GH proto (due EOD 9/13)
- Reach out to Ivy for Console quick mock (copy + preview UI)
- Noam to validate runtime cost model for compressed vs expanded cues

Open parking-lot items:
- Design policy for cue priority (stack ordering vs per-request override precedence)
- Back-compat with customers that embed JSON context in a single instruction block
- UI workflow for sharing stacks across teams with RBAC
- Mini-eval harness to detect quality regressions introduced by compression

Notes to self: rough examples to add later:
- Stack: onboarding-short: {role: "customer-support" (sym: cs), product: "pro-plan", clarity: "concise"}
- Compression experiment: map common phrases -> short tokens ("provide step-by-step" -> "S1") and runtime expands.
summary: Working sketch for a product + runtime feature: Cue Stack Onramp. Focus: compact, reusable micro-context that reduces token bloat and gives teams a first-class way to manage small bits of context via Console + API + runtime merge policies. This doc is a brain dump: API sketches, acceptance criteria, telemetry, risks, and next steps.
